record.title: The conjecture on infinitely many odd-base anti-Niven arithmetic progressions
record.statement:
Let $b$ be an odd integer with $b\neq 2^r+1$ for every positive integer $r$, let $d$ be even, and let $p$ be the smallest prime satisfying $p\mid(b-1)$ and $p\nmid d$. A **$b$-anti-Niven $d$-AP** is an arithmetic progression of integers with common difference $d$ whose terms are relatively prime to their base-$b$ digital sums.

**Anti-Niven progression conjecture.** There exist infinitely many $b$-anti-Niven $d$-APs of length $p-1$.

This conjecture generalizes the result for two-term progressions to other even common differences. The paper provides computational motivation, but no resolution is given.
record.source_name: Ryan Blau, Joshua Harrington, Sarah Lohrey, Eliel Sosis and Tony W. H. Wong, “Arithmetic progressions of integers that are relatively prime to their digital sums”, arXiv:2308.05228 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.05228

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2023).

record.title: Largest anticanonical volume conjecture for Gorenstein terminal Fano varieties
record.statement:
For each odd integer $n\geq5$, let $s_i$ be the sequence used in the paper, and let $X$ be the $n$-fold in the theorem constructing the Gorenstein terminal weighted projective space. **Largest-volume conjecture for Gorenstein terminal Fano varieties.** The anticanonical volume

$$
(-K_X)^n=2^{\frac{n+1}{2}}(s_{\frac{n-1}{2}}-1)^4
$$

of $X$ is the largest possible volume among all Gorenstein terminal Fano $n$-folds. The constructed examples have the largest volume among the corresponding Gorenstein terminal weighted projective spaces in the listed odd dimensions, but optimality for all Gorenstein terminal Fano varieties remains open.
record.source_name: Chengxi Wang, “Fano varieties with conjecturally largest Fano index”, arXiv:2308.06563 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.06563

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2023).

record.title: Budden and DeJonge's star-critical Ramsey conjecture for stars
record.statement:
Let $t\geq 2$ be an integer, and let $m_{1},\dots,m_{t}$ be integers larger than one, exactly $k$ of which are even. For graphs $H_{1},\dots,H_{t}$, the star-critical Ramsey number $r_{*}(H_{1},\dots,H_{t})$ is the minimum integer $k$ such that $K_{N}-K_{1,N-1-k}\rightarrow(H_{1},\dots,H_{t})$, where $N=r(H_{1},\dots,H_{t})$. **Budden and DeJonge's conjecture.**

$$
r_{*}(K_{1,m_{1}},\dots,K_{1,m_{t}})=\begin{cases}\sum_{i=1}^{t}m_{i}-t,&\text{if }k\geq 2\text{ is even},\\1,&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
$$

This conjecture gives the proposed star-critical Ramsey numbers for arbitrary collections of stars, extending the known ordinary Ramsey-number formula of Burr and Roberts. The supplied source does not indicate whether the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Zhidan Luo, “Star-critical Ramsey numbers and regular Ramsey numbers for stars”, arXiv:2308.07194 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07194

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2023).

record.title: The minimal-volume conjecture for log canonical pairs with reduced boundary
record.statement: Let $(X,B)$ be a projective log canonical pair of dimension $n$, where $B$ is a nonzero reduced divisor and $K_X+B$ is ample. The volume of $K_X+B$ is the top self-intersection number $(K_X+B)^n$. The paper constructs such a pair in every dimension, with volume as described in Theorem 1. **Minimal-volume conjecture.** For every integer $n\geq 2$, the constructed pair has the smallest volume among all projective log canonical pairs $(X,B)$ of dimension $n$ with $B$ a nonzero reduced divisor and $K_X+B$ ample. The surface case is known, while the assertion in higher dimensions remains open.
record.source_name: Louis Esser and Burt Totaro, “Log canonical pairs with conjecturally minimal volume”, arXiv:2308.08034 (2026).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.08034

record.title: The dimensions conjecture for fixed subspaces of the Cartier operator
record.statement:
Let $R\in\mathbb{F}_q[z]$ have degree at least $1$ and not be divisible by $z$, and write

$$
R=cR_1^{e_1}\cdots R_k^{e_k}
$$

for its factorization into irreducibles. Define $\lambda_0(S)=\Lambda_0(SR^{q-1})$. For a positive integer $m$, consider the vector space of polynomials $S\in\mathbb{F}_q[z]$ satisfying $\deg S\leq\deg R$ and $\lambda_0^m(S)=S$.

**The dimensions conjecture.** For every divisor $m$ of $\operatorname{lcm}(\deg R_1,\dots,\deg R_k)$, this vector space has dimension

$$
1+\sum_{i=1}^k\gcd(m,\deg R_i).
$$

In particular, the predicted dimension is independent of the exponents $e_i$. The conjecture would determine the period bound for the corresponding orbit under $\lambda_0$, but its status is not resolved in the source.
record.source_name: Eric Rowland, Manon Stipulanti and Reem Yassawi, “An elementary proof of Bridy's theorem”, arXiv:2308.10977 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.10977

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2023).

record.title: Signless Brouwer conjecture for graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices, and let $S_k(G)$ denote the sum of the $k$ largest signless Laplacian eigenvalues of $G$:

$$
S_k(G)=\sum_{i=n+1-k}^{n}\lambda_i(Q(G)).
$$

**Signless Brouwer conjecture.** For an integer $k$ with $1\leq k\leq n$,

$$
S_k(G)\leq |E|+{k+1\choose 2}.
$$

This conjecture is the signless-Laplacian analogue of Brouwer's conjecture for the sum of the largest Laplacian eigenvalues, and has been studied by many researchers. The source discusses it in the context of threshold graphs, but the stated conjecture concerns arbitrary graphs.
record.source_name: Christoph Helmberg, Guilherme Porto, Guilherme Torres and Vilmar Trevisan, “An interlacing property of the signless Laplacian of threshold graphs”, arXiv:2308.12654 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.12654

record.title: The critical-snark defect-3 conjecture
record.statement: Let a **critical snark** be a snark in which deleting any edge yields a $3$-edge-colourable graph, and let the colouring defect of a cubic graph be the minimum number of uncovered edges left by three perfect matchings. **Critical-snark defect-3 conjecture.** Every critical snark has defect $3$. This is motivated by computations showing that critical snarks of order at most $36$ have the asserted defect; whether the claim holds in general remains open.
record.source_name: Ján Karabáš, Edita Máčajová, Roman Nedela and Martin Škoviera, “Cubic graphs with colouring defect 3”, arXiv:2308.13639 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.13639

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of August 2023). “Jaeger conjectured that there exist no (nontrivial) snarks of girth greater than 6, which was later disproved by Kochol in .”

record.title: The linear covering-set conjecture for generalized shuffle squares
record.statement:
Fix an alphabet of size $k$. Let $E_n$ be the set of all even $k$-ary words of length $n$, and let $S_n$ be the set of all permutations of $[n]$. Define $m_k(n)$ to be the minimum size of a set of permutations whose associated shuffle squares cover every word in $E_n$. **The linear covering-set conjecture.** For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$ there exists a constant $c_k$ such that

$$
m_k(n)\leqslant c_kn
$$

for all $n\geqslant 1$. The known binary bound is linear, and the conjecture asks for an analogous linear bound for every fixed alphabet size; it remains open.
record.source_name: Jarosław Grytczuk, Bartłomiej Pawlik and Mariusz Pleszczyński, “Variations on shuffle squares”, arXiv:2308.13882 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.13882

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of August 2023).

record.title: The shuffle anti-square existence conjecture
record.statement: For a binary even word $W$ of length $2n$, let $s(W)$ be the number of circular shifts of $W$ that are shuffle squares. Let $s_{2n}$ be the minimum of $s(W)$ over all binary even words of length $2n$. A **shuffle anti-square** is a binary even word for which no circular shift is a shuffle square. **The shuffle anti-square existence conjecture.** There exists a shuffle anti-square of length $2n$ for every $n\geqslant12$. Equivalently, $s_{2n}=0$ for every $n\geqslant12$. Computational data establish this for the listed small values but do not prove the assertion for all $n\geqslant12$; the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Jarosław Grytczuk, Bartłomiej Pawlik and Mariusz Pleszczyński, “Variations on shuffle squares”, arXiv:2308.13882 (2024).
record.references:

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of August 2023).

record.title: Bessenrodt–Panova conjecture on self-conjugate partitions
record.statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let a partition be **self-conjugate** if it equals its conjugate. Its Durfee size is the side length of its largest square contained in its Young diagram. **Bessenrodt–Panova conjecture.** For every $n$, there exists $k(n)$ such that the tensor square of every self-conjugate partition of $n$ whose Durfee size is at least $k(n)$ and which is not the $k\times k$ partition satisfies the Tensor Square Conjecture. The source presents this as a conjecture about the shapes whose tensor squares contain every irreducible representation, and gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Chenchen Zhao, “On the Kronecker product of Schur functions of square shapes”, arXiv:2309.00764 (2023).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2306.17511](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.17511), [arXiv:2305.02553](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.02553).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.00764

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

record.title: Generalised Erdős–Lax inequality for powers of polynomials
record.statement:
Let

$$
P(z)=c\prod_{k=1}^{N}(z-a_k)^{ms_k},
$$

where $c\in\mathbb{C}$, $m\in\mathbb{N}$, $s_k\geq 1$, $ms_k\in\mathbb{N}$, and $|a_k|\geq 1$. For any branch $f(z)=P(z)^{1/m}$, write $\|\cdot\|_{\mathbb{T}}$ for the maximum modulus on the unit circle. **Generalised Erdős–Lax conjecture.** One has

$$
\|f'\|_{\mathbb{T}}\leq \frac{\sum_{k=1}^{N}s_k}{2}\|f\|_{\mathbb{T}},
$$

with equality if and only if $|a_k|=1$ for all $k$.

This would extend the Erdős–Lax inequality to powers of polynomials without restrictions on the zeros in the exterior of the closed unit disk; the source presents it as conjectural and gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Alex Bergman and Olof Rubin, “Chebyshev polynomials corresponding to a vanishing weight”, arXiv:2309.02047 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.02047

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of September 2023).

record.title: Cambie–de Verclos–Kang conjecture on triangles in regular graphs
record.statement:
For positive integers $n$ and $k$, let $t(n,k)$ be the minimum number of triangles over all $k$-regular graphs on $n$ vertices. Let $\mathcal{G}(n,k)$ denote the family of extremal graphs referred to in the source.

**Cambie–de Verclos–Kang conjecture.** For every odd integer $n$ and even integer $k$ with

$$
\frac{2n}{5}< k< \frac{n}{2},
$$

$$
t(n,k)=\frac{k}{4}(3k-n-1).
$$

Moreover, the extremal graphs must belong to $\mathcal{G}(n,k)$.

This conjecture seeks the exact minimum number of triangles in regular graphs in the range above, together with a characterization of all extremal graphs. The paper records it as a conjecture of Cambie, de Joannis de Verclos, and Kang; the supplied material gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Jialin He, Xinmin Hou, Jie Ma and Tianying Xie, “Counting triangles in regular graphs”, arXiv:2309.02993 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.02993

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

record.title: Projective-plane extremal conjecture for cross-intersecting hypergraphs
record.statement:
For integers $r,m$, let $g(r,m)$ be the maximum, over all $m$-tuples $(H_1,\ldots,H_m)$ of pairwise cross-intersecting $r$-uniform hypergraphs, of

$$
\min_{1\leqslant i\leqslant m}\tau^*(H_i),
$$

where $\tau^*$ denotes fractional covering number. A projective plane of uniformity $r$ gives the lower bound $g(r,m)\geqslant r-1+1/r$ whenever such a plane exists.

**Projective-plane extremal conjecture.** For $m\geqslant r+2$,

$$
g(r,m)\leqslant r-1+\frac1r,
$$

with equality if and only if there is a projective plane of uniformity $r$.
The conjecture is proved in the source for $r=2$, and the paper proves that the bound holds for every $r$ once $m$ is sufficiently large; the general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Ron Aharoni, Eli Berger, Joseph Briggs, He Guo and Shira Zerbib, “Looms”, arXiv:2309.03735 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.03735

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2023). “The conjecture is open for $r\ge 4$.”

record.title: Pinnable rainbow matching conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{H}=(H_1,\ldots,H_m)$ be a family of $r$-uniform hypergraphs. A **rainbow matching** is a matching containing at most one edge from each $H_i$, and $\nu_R(\mathcal{H})$ is its maximum size. Assume that $\bigcup_{i=1}^mH_i$ is pinnable, meaning that some set meets every edge of the union in exactly one vertex.

**Pinnable rainbow matching conjecture.** If

$$
\tau\left(\bigcup_{i\in I}H_i\right)>(2r-2)(|I|-1)
$$

for every $I\subseteq[m]$, then $\mathcal{H}$ has a full rainbow matching:

$$
\nu_R(\mathcal{H})=m.
$$

This strengthens the earlier rainbow matching conjecture by replacing the common partite structure with pinnability. It remains open.
record.source_name: Ron Aharoni, Eli Berger, Joseph Briggs, He Guo and Shira Zerbib, “Looms”, arXiv:2309.03735 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.03735

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2023). “The conjecture is open for $r\ge 4$.”

record.title: Enomoto–Kaneko–Tuza conjecture for edge-disjoint cycle covers in digraphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a digraph on $n$ vertices. Its **minimum semi-degree** is the minimum, over all vertices, of the smaller of its indegree and outdegree. A collection of cycles is **edge-disjoint** if no directed edge belongs to more than one cycle, and it covers $V(G)$ if every vertex lies on one of the cycles.

**Directed edge-disjoint cycle-cover conjecture.** For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$ with $k\geq 2$, if the minimum semi-degree of $G$ is at least $n/k$, then $V(G)$ can be covered by $k-1$ edge-disjoint cycles.

This is proposed as a directed analogue of the Enomoto–Kaneko–Tuza conjecture for graphs. The paper proves the assertion for regular digraphs through its main theorem, while the general digraph statement remains open in the source.
record.source_name: Allan Lo, Viresh Patel and Mehmet Akif Yıldız, “Cycle Partitions in Dense Regular Digraphs and Oriented Graphs”, arXiv:2309.11677 (2025).

record.title: The split-permutation conjecture for largest MVP fibre size
record.statement: For $n\geq 1$, let $\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{MVP}_{n}}$ denote the MVP outcome map on permutations of size $n$, and let $\mathrm{split}^{2,n-2}:=(n-1)n(n-2)(n-3)\cdots21$ for $n\geq3$. The **MVP split-permutation conjecture.** For $n\geq6$, the permutation with the largest MVP fibre size is the split permutation $\mathrm{split}^{2,n-2}$. Numerical evidence supports the claim for $n=7,8,9,10,11$, although the conjecture is not established in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Thomas Selig and Haoyue Zhu, “New combinatorial perspectives on MVP parking functions and their outcome map”, arXiv:2309.11788 (2023).

record.title: Gharakhloo–Welker upper-bound conjecture for positive matching decomposition numbers
record.statement:
Let $H=(V,E)$ be a $3$-uniform hypergraph with $n$ vertices. Its **positive matching decomposition number** $\operatorname{pmd}(H)$ is the smallest number of parts in a positive matching decomposition of $H$.

**Gharakhloo–Welker's conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{pmd}(H)\leq \frac{3}{2}n^2-\frac{15}{2}n+10.
$$

This conjecture proposes a quadratic upper bound for the positive matching decomposition number of every $3$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. The cited source provides no resolution evidence, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Marie Amalore Nambi and Neeraj Kumar, “On Positive Matching Decomposition Conjectures of Hypergraphs”, arXiv:2309.15424 (2025).

record.title: The value of the minimum size for minimal uncolorable triple bi-hypergraphs of order seven
record.statement:
For a bi-hypergraph, a proper coloring assigns colors so that every edge contains more than one color and is not monochromatic. Let $\ell(n,r)$ denote the minimum number of edges in a minimal uncolorable $r$-uniform bi-hypergraph of order $n$.

**Conjecture on $\ell(7,3)$.**

$$
\ell(7,3)=11.
$$

The preceding results establish $10\le \ell(7,3)\le 11$. Thus the conjecture is equivalent to the nonexistence of a minimal uncolorable $3$-uniform bi-hypergraph of order $7$ with $10$ edges; the supplied text gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Meiqiao Zhang, Fengming Dong and Ruixue Zhang, “On the colorability of bi-hypergraphs”, arXiv:2310.06464 (2023).

record.title: Cranston et al.'s quantitative planar Turán conjecture for cycles
record.statement:
Let $C_k$ denote the cycle of length $k$, and let $\operatorname{ex}_{\mathcal P}(n,C_k)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex planar graph containing no subgraph isomorphic to $C_k$. **Cranston et al.'s quantitative conjecture.** There is a constant $D$ such that for all $k$ and all sufficiently large $n$,

$$
\operatorname{ex}_{\mathcal P}(n,C_k)\leq 3n-\frac{Dn}{k^{\log_2 3}}.
$$

This weaker conjecture is proposed because the stronger construction conjecture is difficult to prove; the supplied text gives no resolution of this weaker statement.
record.source_name: Ruilin Shi, Zach Walsh and Xingxing Yu, “Dense circuit graphs and the planar Turán number of a cycle”, arXiv:2310.06631 (2023).

record.title: Optimal minimum-degree conjecture for Tverberg partition graphs
record.statement:
Let $S$ be a set of $n$ points in $\mathds{R}^d$ in **strong general position**, and let $G_T[S,r]$ be its Tverberg $r$-partition graph. Write $\delta(G_T[S,r])$ for the minimum degree of this graph, and let

$$
\operatorname{Tv}(d,r)=(d+1)(r-1)+1.
$$

For $n>\operatorname{Tv}(d,r)$, **the minimum-degree conjecture.** The minimum degree is

$$
\delta(G_T[S,r])=(n+1-\operatorname{Tv}(d,r))(r-1).
$$

The paper has established lower and upper degree bounds, and this conjecture asserts that the lower bound is attained for every strongly general-position configuration. Its resolution is not given in the source.
record.source_name: Deborah Oliveros, Érika Roldán, Pablo Soberón and Antonio J. Torres, “Tverberg Partition Graphs”, arXiv:2310.08563 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08563

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2023). “For example, even finding optimal lower bounds for the number of Tverberg partitions when $|S|=(d+1)(r-1)+1$ is a longstanding open problem that is known as Sierksma's conjecture .”

record.title: The one-fifth conjecture for isolated cycles in connected graphs
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}_4=\{C_k\colon k\geq 4\}$, and let $\iota(G,\mathcal{C}_4)$ denote the maximum number of vertex-disjoint members of $\mathcal{C}_4$ in a graph $G$. Problem 3 asks for the smallest real number $c$, if it exists, such that there is a finite set $\mathcal{E}$ of graphs satisfying

$$
\iota(G,\mathcal{C}_4)\leq c\lvert V(G)\rvert
$$

for every connected graph $G$ that is not an $\mathcal{E}$-graph. **One-fifth conjecture.** The number $c$ in this problem is $1/5$. This conjecture extends the bound for isolating squares in connected graphs to the family of cycles of length at least four, up to excluding a finite set of exceptional graphs; the surrounding text presents it as an open problem.
record.source_name: Karl Bartolo, Peter Borg and Dayle Scicluna, “Isolation of squares in graphs”, arXiv:2310.09128 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.09128

record.title: Alon–Shapira–Sudakov conjecture on the complexity of graph removal
record.statement: Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs, and let $\mathrm{Rem}_H(G)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $H$-free spanning subgraph of $G$. A graph $H$ is a **star forest** if every connected component of $H$ is a star. **Alon–Shapira–Sudakov conjecture.** Computing $\mathrm{Rem}_H(G)$ is NP-hard if and only if $H$ is not a star forest. The theorem preceding this conjecture establishes the corresponding classification for forests; the conjecture asks whether the same dichotomy holds for all graphs $H$.
record.source_name: Lior Gishboliner, Yevgeny Levanzov and Asaf Shapira, “Trimming forests is hard (unless they are made of stars)”, arXiv:2310.11277 (2023).

record.title: Choosability with weak diameter for bounded layered tree-width
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $w$ be a positive integer. A graph is **3-choosable with weak diameter at most $N$** if every list assignment of lists of size $3$ admits a coloring such that each monochromatic component has weak diameter at most $N$ in $G$.

**Layered-tree-width weak-diameter conjecture.** For every positive integer $w$, there exists a positive integer $N$ such that every graph with layered tree-width at most $w$ is 3-choosable with weak diameter in $G$ at most $N$.

This is a stronger-looking list-colouring assertion than bounded clustering in the absence of a maximum-degree hypothesis. The supplied text does not report a resolution.
record.source_name: Joshua Crouch and Chun-Hung Liu, “Weak diameter choosability of graphs with an excluded minor”, arXiv:2310.17795 (2025).

record.title: The zero forcing lower bound for Cartesian products
record.statement:
Let $G$ and $G'$ be graphs, each containing an edge. The **Cartesian-product zero forcing conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{Z}(G\Box G')\geq \operatorname{Z}(G)\operatorname{Z}(G')+1.
$$

The conjecture would extend the sharp lower bound known when the maximum nullity equals the zero forcing number for both factors to arbitrary graphs containing an edge. Together with the standard upper bound for Cartesian products, it would give a general Vizing-like constraint on the zero forcing number.
record.source_name: Thomas R. Cameron, Leslie Hogben, Franklin H. J. Kenter, Seyed Ahmad Mojallal and Houston Schuerger, “Forts, (fractional) zero forcing, and Cartesian products of graphs”, arXiv:2310.17904 (2026).

record.title: Conjecture on maximizers of r-star for n divisible by four
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $r_\star$ be the maximum value of the $r$-loading over triples of partitions of $n$. For a partition, notation such as $(k^4)$ means four parts equal to $k$, and $(2^{2k})$ means $2k$ parts equal to $2$.

**Maximizer conjecture for $r_\star$.** When $n=4k$ with $k\ge 2$, the values $r_\star$ are attained by

$$
\mathbf t=((k^4),(2^{2k}),(2^{2k})).
$$

The conjecture is inferred from the cases $n=8,12,16,20$ displayed in the paper; no proof or resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Kyu-Hwan Lee, “Data-scientific study of Kronecker coefficients”, arXiv:2310.17906 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.17906

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).

record.title: Conjecture on maximizers of b-star
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $b_\star$ be the maximum value of the $b$-loading over triples $\mathbf t=(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$ of partitions of $n$.

**Maximizer conjecture for $b_\star$.** For $n\ge 6$, the values $b_\star$ are attained by triples such that

$$
\lambda=\mu\quad\text{or}\quad\mu=\nu.
$$

Moreover, when $n=3k$ with $k\ge 2$, the values $b_\star$ are attained by triples such that

$$
\lambda=\mu=\nu.
$$

The conjecture is based on the tabulated cases, particularly $n=6,9,12,15,18$; no proof or resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Kyu-Hwan Lee, “Data-scientific study of Kronecker coefficients”, arXiv:2310.17906 (2024).

record.title: Biclique-intersection improvement conjecture
record.statement:
For a fixed graph $H$, let $g_H(n)$ be the maximum size of an $H$-intersecting family of graphs on $[n]$. **Biclique-intersection conjecture.** There exist $t\in\mathbb{N}$ and an absolute constant $c>0$ such that

$$
g_{K_{t,t}}(n)\leq(1-c)2^{\binom n2-1}
$$

for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$. The source describes this as a weaker open problem related to improving the trivial upper bound for bipartite graphs.

record.title: Modular Rado boundedness conjecture
record.statement:
For $k\in\mathbb{N}$, let $a_1,\ldots,a_k\in\mathbb{Z}/(2^r\mathbb{Z})$, and let $d\leq r$ be the largest non-negative integer such that $2^d$ divides $\sum_{i\in I}a_i$ for some non-empty $I\subseteq[k]$. **Modular Rado boundedness conjecture.** There exists $K\in\mathbb{N}$, depending only on $k$, such that one can $K$-colour $\mathbb{Z}/(2^r\mathbb{Z})$ so that every monochromatic solution $x=(x_1,\ldots,x_k)$ of

$$
a_1x_1+\cdots+a_kx_k=0
$$

satisfies $2^{r-d}\mid x_i$ for every $i\in[k]$. The source notes that a compactness argument would imply the single-equation case of Rado's boundedness conjecture.

record.title: Order-$k$ Delaunay triangulations maximize triangles among local-angle hypertriangulations
record.statement:
Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be finite and generic. For every $1 \leq k \leq |A|-1$, let $\mathcal{F}_k$ be the family of level-$k$ hypertriangulations that have the local angle property, and let $P_k \in \mathcal{F}_k$.

**Order-$k$ Delaunay optimality conjecture.** The hypertriangulation $P_k$ has the maximum number of triangles if and only if $P_k$ is the order-$k$ Delaunay triangulation of $A$.

The result is known for order $2$ among complete level-$2$ hypertriangulations, whereas higher orders and broader classes of competing hypertriangulations remain open.
record.source_name: Herbert Edelsbrunner, Alexey Garber and Morteza Saghafian, “Order-2 Delaunay Triangulations Optimize Angles”, arXiv:2310.18238 (2024).

record.title: Minimum-semidegree conjecture for bounded-degree spanning oriented trees
record.statement: Let $\Delta\in\mathbb N$, and let $c$ be a constant. **The bounded-degree spanning-tree conjecture.** For every $\Delta$ there is a $c$ such that every sufficiently large $n$-vertex digraph with minimum semidegree at least $n/2+c\log n$ contains every $n$-vertex oriented tree of maximum total degree at most $\Delta$. This is presented as a missing directed analogue of a graph theorem and remains open.
record.source_name: Maya Stein, “Oriented trees and paths in digraphs”, arXiv:2310.18719 (2024).

record.title: Felsner–Weil connectivity conjecture for flip graphs of signotopes
record.statement: An $r$-signotope is a mapping from the $r$-subsets of an $n$-element set to $\\{+,-\\}$ satisfying the relevant monotonicity condition, and a flip changes the sign of a single $r$-set. Let $\mathbf{G}^r_n$ be the flip graph of $r$-signotopes on $n$ elements. **Felsner–Weil conjecture.** For every $r\ge 3$, the flip graph $\mathbf{G}^r_n$ has minimum degree $n-r+1$ and is $(n-r+1)$-connected. The cases $r=1$ and $r=2$ are known, corresponding respectively to hypercubes and permutahedra; the assertion for higher ranks remains unresolved.
record.source_name: Yan Alves Radtke, Stefan Felsner, Johannes Obenaus, Sandro Roch, Manfred Scheucher and Birgit Vogtenhuber, “Flip Graph Connectivity for Arrangements of Pseudolines and Pseudocircles”, arXiv:2310.19711 (2023).

record.title: Allcock's Bimonster covering conjecture
record.statement:
A 13-dimensional complex ball quotient is obtained from the Allcock lattice construction, with $X$ denoting the corresponding ball quotient and $X^{\rm sg}$ its singular or special-locus pair. **Allcock's conjecture.** The universal reflection Galois group of the pair $(X,X^{\rm sg})$ is isomorphic to the Bimonster

$$
{\mathbf M}\wr\mu_2=({\mathbf M}\times{\mathbf M})\rtimes\mu_2,
$$

where ${\mathbf M}$ is the Monster, the largest sporadic simple group. This is the precise covering-group formulation of Allcock's proposal for the natural Bimonster covering of the 13-dimensional ball quotient; the supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Eduard Looijenga, “Cubic threefolds moduli and the Monster group”, arXiv:2310.20124 (2024).
record.references:

record.title: Mohar's HL-index conjecture for planar subcubic graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph of order $n$, and let its adjacency eigenvalues be 
$$
\lambda_1(G)\ge\dots\ge\lambda_n(G).
$$
 A graph is **subcubic** if its maximum degree is at most $3$, and it is **planar** if it can be drawn in the plane without edge crossings. Define the HL-index by 
$$
R(G)=\max\left\{|\lambda_h(G)|,|\lambda_l(G)|\right\},
$$
 where 
$$
h=\left\lfloor\frac{n+1}{2}\right\rfloor,\qquad l=\left\lceil\frac{n+1}{2}\right\rceil.
$$
 **Mohar's HL-index conjecture.** For every subcubic planar graph $G$, 
$$
R(G)\le 1.
$$
 Mohar proved the weaker bound $R(G)\le\sqrt{2}$ for every subcubic graph. The conjecture asserts the sharper bound for planar subcubic graphs and remains unresolved based on the supplied text.
record.source_name: Yuzhenni Wang and Xiao-Dong Zhang, “A note on median eigenvalues of subcubic graphs”, arXiv:2311.01884 (2023).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2023). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1309.7395](https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.7395).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.01884

record.title: Caputo's shuffle conjecture for weighted hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite weighted hypergraph with non-negative weights. At each step, choose a hyper-edge with probability proportional to its weight and then choose a uniformly random permutation of the vertices in that hyper-edge. Let $\lambda_2^{\mathrm{RW}}(G)$ and $\lambda_2^{\mathrm{IP}}(G)$ be the second-largest eigenvalues of the corresponding random-walk and interchange-process transition operators. **Caputo's conjecture.** For every such $G$,

$$
\lambda_{2}^{\mathrm{RW}}(G)=\lambda_{2}^{\mathrm{IP}}(G).
$$

This is the proposed hypergraph generalization of the Aldous--Caputo--Liggett--Richthammer theorem. The supplied source gives no resolution status for the conjecture.

record.title: The maximal edge-length sum conjecture for full grid lattice polygons
record.statement:
Let $a(n)$ be the maximum of the sum of the squares of the edge-lengths over full grid lattice polygons with $n$ vertices, and let $\alpha(n)$ be the explicit lower-bound function defined in the preceding result. **Maximal edge-length sum conjecture.** For $n\geq 9$, 

$$
a(n)=\alpha(n).
$$

The conjecture asserts that the construction achieving $\alpha(n)$ is optimal for every $n\geq 9$; the supplied text gives no resolution, so the claim remains open.
record.source_name: Oliver Mantas Ališauskas, Giedrius Alkauskas and Valdas Dičiūnas, “Full Grid Lattice Polygons with Maximal Sum of Squares of Edge-Lengths”, arXiv:2311.03011 (2024).

record.title: Mixed-graph pseudo-dicut orientation threshold conjecture
record.statement:
Let $M=(V,E\cup A)$ be a mixed graph, with directed arcs $A$ and undirected edges $E$. For $U\subset V$, a **pseudo dicut** is $\delta_E(U)$ when no directed arc enters $U$. Its **minimum pseudo dicut size** is the smallest cardinality of a pseudo dicut.

**Mixed-graph threshold orientation conjecture.** There is a constant $k>2$ such that every mixed graph with minimum pseudo dicut size at least $k$ has an orientation $E^+$ satisfying

$$
|\delta_{E^+}^+(U)|,|\delta_{E^+}^-(U)|\geq 1
$$

for every pseudo dicut $\delta_E(U)$.

This is presented as a weaker question than the preceding mixed-graph orientation conjecture; the source gives no resolution.

record.title: The logarithmic quantitative sumset conjecture
record.statement:
For $\delta>0$ and $N\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\phi(\delta,N)$ be the largest integer such that every set $A\subset\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with $|A|\geq\delta N$ contains $B+C$, where $B,C\subset\{1,\ldots,N\}$ satisfy $\min\{|B|,|C|\}\geq\phi(\delta,N)$.

**Quantitative sumset conjecture.** For every $\delta>0$,

$$
\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{\phi(\delta,N)}{\log N}<\infty
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{\phi(\delta,N)}{\log N}>0.
$$

The source notes that $\phi(\delta,N)\to\infty$ for fixed $\delta$, and conjectures that its order of growth is logarithmic.
record.source_name: Bryna Kra, Joel Moreira, Florian K. Richter and Donald Robertson, “Problems on infinite sumset configurations in the integers and beyond”, arXiv:2311.06197 (2025).

record.title: The exceptional Thurston–Bennequin conjecture for the knot $9_{42}$
record.statement:
For a strongly invertible Legendrian knot, let its Thurston–Bennequin number be denoted by $\operatorname{tb}$, let $\overline{\operatorname{tb}}(K)$ be the maximal Thurston–Bennequin number among Legendrian representatives of a knot type $K$, and let $\overline{\operatorname{tb}}_e(K)$ be the corresponding maximum restricted to strongly invertible Legendrian representatives. **The $9_{42}$ Thurston–Bennequin conjecture.**

$$
\overline{\operatorname{tb}}_e(9_{42})<\overline{\operatorname{tb}}(9_{42}).
$$

This is based on experiments showing that the maximal known representative of $9_{42}$ is not strongly invertible; the claim remains an experimental conjecture.
record.source_name: Carlo Collari and Paolo Lisca, “Strongly Invertible Legendrian Links”, arXiv:2311.07974 (2023).

record.title: Directional maximum conjecture for the logarithmic derivative of the Riemann zeta function
record.statement:
Fix $\epsilon\in(0,\frac12)$. For $T>0$, consider the interval $[T,2T]$, and let $\zeta(s)$ denote the Riemann zeta function. **Directional maximum conjecture.** As $T\to\infty$, 

$$
\max_{T\le t\le 2T}\operatorname{Re}\left(e^{-\mathrm{i}\theta}\frac{\zeta'}{\zeta}(\sigma+\mathrm{i}t)\right)\sim\frac{\displaystyle\max_{T\le t\le 2T}|\zeta'(\sigma+\mathrm{i}t)|}{\displaystyle\max_{T\le t\le 2T}|\zeta(\sigma+\mathrm{i}t)|},
$$

uniformly for all $\theta\in[0,2\pi]$ and all $\sigma\in[\frac12+\epsilon,1]$. The source presents this as the zeta-function analogue of the preceding Dirichlet $L$-function conjecture and gives no evidence of a resolution.
record.source_name: Daodao Yang, “Omega theorems for logarithmic derivatives of zeta and L-functions”, arXiv:2311.16371 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.16371

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2023).

record.title: Central-line maximal logarithmic derivative conjecture for Dirichlet $L$-functions
record.statement:
Let $q$ tend to infinity through the primes. For a prime $q$, let $\chi_0$ be the principal character modulo $q$, and let $L(s,\chi)$ be the Dirichlet $L$-function associated with $\chi$. Write $\log_2 q=\log\log q$. **Central-line maximal logarithmic derivative conjecture.** There exist constants $A>0$ and $D>\frac12$ such that, as prime $q\to\infty$,

$$
\max_{\substack{\chi\neq\chi_0\\ \chi\ (\operatorname{mod} q)}}\operatorname{Re}\left(e^{-\mathrm{i}\theta}\frac{L'}{L}\left(\frac12,\chi\right)\right)\sim A\sqrt{\log q}(\log_2 q)^D,
$$

uniformly for all $\theta\in[0,2\pi]$. This conjectures the scale of the largest directional logarithmic derivative at the central point, with the constants constrained only by $A>0$ and $D>\frac12$; no resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Daodao Yang, “Omega theorems for logarithmic derivatives of zeta and L-functions”, arXiv:2311.16371 (2023).

record.title: The classification conjecture for unit reducible cyclotomic fields
record.statement: Let $K_N=\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_N)$ be the cyclotomic field of conductor $N$, where $\zeta_N$ is a primitive $N$th root of unity. A cyclotomic field is **unit reducible** if it has the unit-reducibility property defined in the paper. **The authors' conjecture.** The cyclotomic fields $K_N$ where $N=3,4,5,7,8,9,11,12,15,20,21,24$ are the only unit reducible cyclotomic fields. Determining the complete list of unit reducible cyclotomic fields is the principal open problem identified by the authors; the paper establishes that only finitely many such fields exist but does not determine the entire list.

record.title: Waiter–Client tree-universality conjecture
record.statement: Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices. A graph is **tree-universal at degree bound** $D$ if it contains a copy of every tree $T$ with $n$ vertices and maximum degree $\Delta(T)\leq D$. **Waiter–Client tree-universality conjecture.** There exists a constant $c>0$ such that, for every sufficiently large integer $n$, in the $(1:1)$ Waiter–Client game on $K_n$, Waiter has a strategy forcing Client to claim a graph that is tree-universal at degree bound $cn$. The source says that the established degree order in the Waiter–Client theorem should be improvable, but gives no resolution of this conjecture.

record.title: The odd-bridge conjecture for 2-linear trees
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a $2$-linear tree, and let its bridge be the distinguished path joining its two linear components. Write $\operatorname{Max}(T)$ for the set of maximum arrangements of $T$, and $\operatorname{MaxBip}(T)$ for the set of maximal bipartite arrangements of $T$.

**Odd-bridge conjecture.** If the bridge of $T$ has odd length, then no maximal non-bipartite arrangement is a maximum arrangement; equivalently,

$$
\operatorname{Max}(T)=\operatorname{MaxBip}(T).
$$

The conjecture is motivated by exhaustive data showing that odd-bridge $2$-linear trees of the tested orders are maximizable only by bipartite arrangements. A proof for all such trees is not supplied.
record.source_name: Lluís Alemany-Puig, Juan Luis Esteban and Ramon Ferrer-i-Cancho, “Maximum Linear Arrangement: exact algorithms for specific classes of graphs and approximation algorithms for wide classes of graphs”, arXiv:2312.04487 (2026).

record.title: Briançon–Iarrobino conjecture on maximal tangent spaces of punctual Hilbert schemes
record.statement:
Let $N\geq 1$ and let $\mathfrak{m}=(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\subset\mathbb{C}[x_1,\ldots,x_N]$. **Briançon–Iarrobino conjecture.** The ideal $\mathfrak{m}^k$ has the maximum dimension tangent space among all elements of

$$
\operatorname{Hilb}^{\binom{N-1+k}{N}}(\mathbb{A}^N).
$$

This is described as a well-known long-standing conjecture, attributed in the source to Briançon and Iarrobino (1978); the source does not state a resolution.

record.title: Spiro's clique Ramsey-number conjecture
record.statement:
Let $r_F(H)$ denote the minimum number of copies of $F$ in a graph that is $H$-Ramsey, meaning that every two-coloring of its edges contains a monochromatic copy of $H$. For a complete graph $K_s$, write $r_{K_s}(K_t)$ for this quantity, and let $r(K_t)$ be the ordinary Ramsey number of $K_t$.

**Spiro's conjecture.** For all $s\leq t$,

$$
r_{K_s}(K_t)=\binom{r(K_t)}s.
$$

This conjecture asks whether the precise relationship between the Ramsey number and the size Ramsey number of complete graphs extends from copies of edges to copies of every complete graph $K_s$.

record.title: Quasi-transitive bounded-crossing conjecture for coarse planarity
record.statement:
A graph is **quasi-transitive** if its automorphism group has finitely many vertex orbits. Its **local crossing number** is the maximum number of crossings involving any one edge in a plane drawing. A graph has bounded degree if its vertex degrees are uniformly bounded.

**Bounded-crossing conjecture.** Every quasi-transitive graph of bounded local crossing number and degree is quasi-isometric to a planar graph.

The source presents this as a variant of its main theorem for $k$-planar graphs and notes that it would imply a positive answer to another problem. The conjecture is not resolved in the supplied text.

record.title: The six-point MST-ratio conjecture for planar point sets
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a set of $n$ points in the plane. Write $w(P)$ for the length of a Euclidean minimum spanning tree of $P$, and let

$$
\gamma(P)=\max_{P=R\cup B}\frac{w(R)+w(B)}{w(P)},
$$

where the maximum is over all non-trivial bipartitions of $P$ into two sets. **Six-point MST-ratio conjecture.** For any set $P$ of $n\geq 6$ points in the plane, we have $\gamma(P)>1$.
This would improve the paper's established guarantee from $n\geq 12$ to $n\geq 6$; the conjecture is presented as an open question in the source.

record.title: DCC conjecture for volumes of orbifold pairs on rational double points
record.statement:
Let $(X,C)$ be an orbifold pair on a rational double point, where $C$ is a boundary of the form

$$
C=\sum_i (1/n_i)C_i.
$$

**DCC conjecture.** The set of volumes of such orbifold pairs satisfies the descending chain condition, and its minimum nonzero value is

$$
1/3528=(2\cdot 42\cdot 42)^{-1}.
$$

The paper motivates this claim by noting that volumes of general Gorenstein orbifold pairs need not satisfy the DCC, while the restriction to rational double points is expected to restore this property. The supplied context does not state whether the conjecture has been proved or disproved.

record.title: DCC conjecture for volumes of RDP orbifold pairs
record.statement:
Let $(X,C)$ be an orbifold pair on a rational double point, with boundary

$$
C=\sum_i (1/n_i)C_i.
$$

**DCC conjecture.** The set of volumes of these orbifold pairs satisfies the descending chain condition, and its minimum nonzero value is

$$
1/3528=1/(2\cdot 42^2).
$$

This is the proposed restriction to Gorenstein log terminal surface singularities after examples show that volumes of general Gorenstein orbifold pairs can form a strictly decreasing sequence. The supplied context does not state whether the claim has been proved or disproved.

record.title: Arnol'd's Lagrangian intersection conjecture
record.statement: Let $L$ be a closed smooth manifold and let $T^*L$ denote its cotangent bundle. For every compactly supported Hamiltonian diffeomorphism $\phi$ of $T^*L$, consider the intersection points of the zero section $L$ with its image $\phi(L)$. **Arnol'd's conjecture.** The number of intersection points $\phi(L)\cap L$ is bounded from below by the minimal number of critical points of a smooth function on $L$. This is the Lagrangian version of Arnol'd's conjecture for cotangent bundles and motivates lower bounds for Lagrangian intersections; the source does not provide enough information here to determine whether the conjecture has been resolved.
